_description: virtio storage IoTimeoutValue thresholds (KCS-7132512). Single source of truth for the Python analyzer, the PowerShell guest collector/remediation, and the Prometheus recording rule.
_why: M-7: these values previously existed as four uncoordinated magic numbers -- 60 and 180 in insights-rules/plugins/bsod_storage_checks.py, 300 in scripts/collect-windows-guest-info.ps1's remediation, and 60 again in alerts/bsod-risk-recording-rules.yaml. Not contradictory (300 >= 180 passes), but unmanaged: a TSE reading the analyzer learned 'set 180', read the remediation script and found 300, and read the recording rule and found a fourth threshold. Changing guidance required edits in three languages with no test binding them. The repo already enforces this discipline for virtio-win versions via shared/virtio-win-thresholds.json; this extends it.
_windows_default_note: Value assumed by Windows when the Parameters key or IoTimeoutValue is absent. At or below this is the documented danger zone under storage latency spikes (KCS-7132512).
_recommended_min_note: Analyzer PASS threshold. At or above this the VM is considered tuned.
_remediation_target_note: Value written by collect-windows-guest-info.ps1 -Remediate. Deliberately above recommended_min so a remediated guest has headroom rather than sitting exactly on the PASS boundary. Requires a guest reboot to take effect.
_risk_factor_note: Threshold used by bsod:vm_risk_factor_count:gauge in alerts/bsod-risk-recording-rules.yaml. Kept equal to windows_default_seconds: the metric counts VMs still sitting at the untuned default.
